content_selection.rationale: The brief's main stories are well chosen. The Anthropic eval shutdown, the OpenAI grader incident, the White House disclosure statement and Nadella's post make a timely and coherent safety theme, and the OpenAI revenue re-base plus the Broadcom financing, the Nvidia–Reflection talks and the Gemini agent launch are the right industry items. Excluding DevDay/GPT-6.1 Sol was correct, because it happened on Sept 29 and is old news. But three widely covered stories from Oct 8 were dropped, even though the brief covers other Oct 8 items (Gemini, Arena, the fired researchers). Meanwhile, low-value arXiv items found via a recap (the USC guardrail paper, the METR curve re-fit) and Liquid AI's d1 got space. That is a clear but limited miss, not a structural failure.
content_selection.evidence: The brief says 'Quiet on models: release trackers logged no major frontier-model launches from Oct 9 to 11' and keeps room for 'Liquid AI open-sourced d1-3B and d1-omni-600M'. Yet 'OpenAI Dark Clark Russian/Iranian influence-ops disruption' and 'USA Today Co. sues OpenAI for $250M+' are marked [excluded].

selection_disagreements.rationale: OpenAI's Oct 8 report rated Dark Clark Category 5 on the Breakout Scale, the first operation at that level since it began disclosing these cases. Wide coverage (BusinessToday, Qazinform, BigGo, NPR in the candidate list) describes it as the most far-reaching influence operation OpenAI has disrupted. It fits the brief's safety and misuse theme and deserved at least a headline-only note.

selection_disagreements.story: USA Today Co. sues OpenAI for $250M+
selection_disagreements.rationale: Reuters broke the story and many outlets picked it up. USA Today Co. and about 19 affiliated papers filed in SDNY on Oct 8, seeking more than $250M and the destruction of models, and adding a CMI-stripping claim. A major new publisher copyright suit against OpenAI deserved a headline-only line, especially since the brief already runs OpenAI business items.

selection_disagreements.story: Anthropic 2026 Usage Policy update (abuse toward Claude, election/deception rules, high-risk human review) effective Nov 12
selection_disagreements.rationale: Announced Oct 8 and covered by The Register, The Verge (per explainx), Unite.ai, Notebookcheck and AI Weekly. It is Anthropic's first usage policy update in over a year. It drops the blanket ban on personalized campaign targeting, adds a model-abuse clause and new weapons-software and surveillance rules, and requires human review for hiring, lending and claims decisions. That is more consequential for builders than several headline-only items that made the cut.

selection_disagreements.story: Liquid AI d1 open models and the USC open-weight decision-model guardrail paper (arXiv 2610.12292)
selection_disagreements.rationale: These are minor follow-ups to a niche thread. The USC paper reached the brief only through a newsletter recap, and neither item showed broad pickup. Their space would have been better spent on the Dark Clark report or the USA Today lawsuit, both of which had far broader mainstream coverage.

factual_accuracy.rationale: I checked 15 claims against live sources. Thirteen were confirmed on specifics: the Anthropic report and the Philadelphia tip (July 18 / Sept 28 / Oct 7, called "unacceptable"), the OpenAI grader incident (the identical score of 4, fake files, three failed health checks), the 719 manuscripts with only 10 including chain of thought, the FT's "approaching $50B", Broadcom's $50B+ with Apollo and Blackstone, Arena's $200M at $3.1B, Decision-1's $0.042/M price and 35x speed claim, all of Memento 3's headline numbers, InnovationEval's figures, and Nvidia's $800M in Reflection plus Beam's release five days earlier. The brief also correctly hedges what it hasn't confirmed itself, such as the withdrawal of three proofs and the 25 Fields Medalists. Two small details differ from the sources: the brief calls FTC chair Andrew Ferguson a "vice-chair" of the SI Force when the sourcing says co-chair, and it says Nvidia and Reflection "declined to comment" when the coverage says they "did not immediately respond". A few secondary details I couldn't verify, including the Claude Opus 5 baseline of 40.7, the Bloomberg year-end target of $70B or more, and Anthropic briefing the White House.
factual_accuracy.evidence: Brief: "The SI Force is chaired by Jay Clayton, with FTC chair Andrew Ferguson among its vice-chairs" vs explainx/Axios: led by Jay Clayton "with co-chairs Federal Trade Commission chair Andrew Ferguson, ... Scott Kupor, and ... Emil Michael."

length_format.rationale: The counts are within range. The brief has 12 Headlines bullets (target 8-15) and 10 deep-dive items (target 5-10: Research 2, Industry 2, Products 1, Benchmarks 1, Policy 4), uses the required tiered sections, and omits none it needed. The per-item length target is consistently and substantially exceeded, though. Every deep dive runs well past 3-6 sentences: the shortest (Memento 3) has about 8, and the Anthropic and mathematics items run roughly 13-17 sentences each. The structure and counts comply, but the bloated summaries are a meaningful over-shoot of the stated 'dense 3-6 sentence' format.
length_format.evidence: The Anthropic deep dive alone runs from 'In a report titled "Investigating unintended model actions..."' through multiple incident descriptions, police and NYT details, and remediation steps to 'Why it matters...', roughly 15+ sentences against a 3-6 sentence target.

dedup.rationale: Four of today's items overlap with prior editions: the OpenAI math proofs (Oct 7 & Oct 8), AI chip debt (Oct 8), Reflection AI (Oct 9) and decision models (Oct 7 & Oct 9). Each is explicitly labelled as a follow-up or continuing thread and names the prior date. Each also adds substantial new information: the field's critical response and a Cambridge/KCL formalization-gap paper; the FT's revenue re-basing and WSJ's report of Broadcom arranging $50B+ for OpenAI; Nvidia's acquisition talks; and Microsoft Decision-1 and Liquid d1 launches. All other stories (Anthropic eval containment, the White House SI Force statement, OpenAI's grader misalignment report, the fired safety researchers, Google's Gemini agent, Memento 3, InnovationEval, Arena) do not appear in any prior edition.
